title.narrative: CPD Institutional Strengthening to Support Bangladeshs Dual Transition

description.narrative:
To increase awareness among stakeholders including policymakers on the pitfalls of Bangladesh’s dual graduation and necessary changes in policies, measures and operations to be required addressing those through independent research and participatory discussions
This project funding under the 2019 LGA frame is with the Centre for Policy Dialogue (CPD) to support the organization with core funding so that it can strengthen its capacity and conduct policy advocacy and dialogue, research, and participatory outreach in the context of Bangladesh’s ‘‘dual transition’’ in the coming years. The key result is ‘To ensure an inclusive and just society by addressing the pitfalls of Bangladesh’s dual graduation through research, policy dialogue and participatory outreach’. The indicators include: - Improvement in economic, social, environmental and governance indicators; - Institutional and regulatory reforms undertaken by Government of Bangladesh

title.narrative: 1.1. Recommendations made by external auditor are implemented
1.1 statement: CPD has increased sustainability and improved capacity as a think-think during Bangladesh’s dual graduation period

target.value: CPD improved its sustainability and capacity as a leading think tank as per external evaluation

actual.value: - The project contributed to capacity building of researchers in conducting qualitative and quantitative research. The project helped improved efficiency of the Finance Division and led to better financial control internally. - Since CPD does not have an endowment fund, financial sustainability continues to be a challenge. Overhead was covered by CPD, as most donors are reluctant to provide such costs. As CPD believes revenue generation or taking donation from corporates risks conflict of interest and/or diluted focus, they continue to work with non-profit model. - CPD has enhanced project management capacity and resource mobilisation capability: (i) CPD has now increased participation in open call for proposals. This has also improved the possibility of winning research grants; (ii) CPD can deliver project commitments better, has better M&E, and use the learning experiences for future projects. Over the three years, a total of 35 proposals were submitted and 26 accepted

title.narrative: 1.1.2 CPD’s financial management and internal control policies and systems are satisfactory
1.1.2 statement: Strengthened financial management and internal control system and management support system

target.value: -Improved financial control and strengthen financial management

actual.value: - CPD procured and made operational an integrated accounting software - CPD has strengthened and is maintaining a fixed assets register regularly - CPD has strengthened and is maintaining project wise books of accounts - An independent internal auditor was recruited in 2020 and the officer reports directly to the Executive Director as well as prepares quarterly reports for the Audit Committee. - Financial systems were improved. A total of 17 polices in place including procurement policy and anti-corruption policy

target.value: CPD strengthens its financial management and internal control related systems -Independent internal auditor recruited

actual.value: 100% progress CPD has strengthened its financial management and internal control related systems throughout the year. • An independent internal auditor has been recruited and is continuing his work independently since the last year. • The internal auditor prepares periodic reports for the CPD management.

target.value: -New accounting software in place for project-wise accounting -Properly maintained fixed assets register and inventory -Adequate procurement policy in place ? Improved financial control and strengthen financial management

actual.value: CPD appears to have made tangible progress in upgrading their financial management system and internal controls in consistency with good business practice, however, we have some observations and recommendations. Donors and CPD Board may consider our recommendations for further improvement. The practical implementation and compliance of these standards should be regularly monitored. We recommend that according to sound business practice and to avoid any conflict of interest, the Chair of the Audit Committee should be independent from any executive functions in the organization. Also, the existing Charter/ToR of the audit committee should be expanded to articulate the required qualification and experience of the Audit Committee members. The internal auditor needs to undergo training on internal audit methodology and he should report to the audit committee on a quarterly basis.

title.narrative: 1.1.3. statement: Enhanced human resources and organizational performance

target.value: -Staff size adjusted as per strategic plan

actual.value: - Completed five all-staff trainings, one M&E training, four skills trainings, two finance and admin training, one fundraising training - A rationalised staffing plan has been prepared and maintained with an optimal ratio of permanent and contractual staff 54% permanent staff in Nov 2022, reduced from 82% 46% contractual staff in Nov 2022, increased from 18%

target.value: -Assessment of staffing competence and staffing needs to deliver the strategic pathway -Finance staff have improved capacity -Capacity development plan developed for all employees

actual.value: CPD has argued for a premium for exclusive retention of their senior and exceptionally qualified resources. Salaries of positions from the Deputy Director level downwards should be reviewed by a professional HR expert to assess scope for further rationalization, if any. CPD needs to refine and discuss their rationalized staffing plan within themselves and then with the Donor. CPD obtained information on salary scale of two similar organisations, such as BIGD and TIB, and provided comparative summary of 11 positions. Regarding the capacity development plan, a need assessment across all the divisions should be undertaken to properly assess the development needs of individual staff, and proceed accordingly. All professionals are working in the Administration and Finance Division as per Work Plan. Conducted in-house trainings for admin, finance and Project Development, Resource Mobilisation and Learning (PRL) staff

target.value: - Capacity development integrated through improved supervision and/or training - Staff size adjusted as per strategic plan

actual.value: • Training for employee’s capacity development will be held by November 2021. However, they are being closely monitored and supervised by their respective supervisor (Capacity development plan is in Annex Table: 4) • A rationalized staffing plan has been prepared with an optimal ratio of permanent and contractual staff

title.narrative: 1.1.1 External auditor assessed CPD as having improved governance and structure

target.value: Progress in implementation of strategic pathway document

actual.value: - The strategic pathway document was developed and implemented The document presented CPD’s activities in accordance with Bangladesh’s challenges such as LDC graduation by 2026, Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) by 2030, upper-middle income country by 2031 and higher income country by 2041, implantation of the Eighth Five Year Plan (2021-25), and the Perspective Plan for 2041. CPD articulated its target groups to include both global and local policymakers. CPD also highlighted frontier issues, which are critical to the development process of Bangladesh and South Asia from the medium-term perspective. - (i) CPD reviewed existing service rules, policies, organogram, job responsibilities and salary structure; (ii) interviewed key stakeholders finalize the strategic plan. By 2022, CPD implemented activities for research, policy dialogue, finance, fundraising and M&E. A staffing plan was made and staff composition streamlined

target.value: Progress in implementation of strategic pathway document

actual.value: 100% progress (Implemented as per work plan) • The strategic pathway document has been finalized and approved by the board.

target.value: Developed one strategic pathway document for the next five years. Audit Committee properly defined and operational ? A rationalized staffing plan (derived from research plans in the Strategic Pathway document) ? A responsibility matrix for senior and mid management

actual.value: CPD’s policies appear to be sound and consistent with good business practice. Donors and CPD Board may consider our recommendations for further improvement. The practical implementation and compliance of these policies should be regularly monitored.

title.narrative: 2.1 Number of government representatives present at CPD policy dialogues; Number of media coverage of CPD’s policy recommendations;
2.1 statement: Government informed about the challenges and opportunities arising from dual graduation policies through evidence-based research and participatory discussions

target.value: Increased collaboration and engagement with government

actual.value: CPD was able to increase awareness on necessary policy reforms by facilitating independent research and participatory discussions. CPD engaged with over 19 different organizations on policy matters, including major advocacy players, to ensure strengthened policy influencing. CPD’s policy dialogues together with wide range of experts, public officials and the media was effective for advocacy.
